column_semantics: The schedule uses a single Rate (b) column. For variable-rate investments, the printed base-rate spread is the cash/base-rate spread and any PIK component is printed separately in the same rate cell, e.g. in parentheses after the spread. For fixed PIK-only instruments, the rate is printed with PIK after it, meaning the printed percentage is a PIK rate rather than an all-in cash-plus-PIK coupon.

citations.quote: (b) Certain variable rate securities in the Company's portfolio bear interest at a rate determined by a publicly disclosed base rate plus a basis point spread. As of March 31, 2026, the Secured Overnight Financing Rate, or SOFR or "SF", was 3.68 %, the Sterling Overnight Index Average, or SONIA or "SA", was 3.85 % and the Euro Interbank Offered Rate, or EURIBOR or "E", was 2.08 %. PIK means paid-in-kind. PIK income accruals may be adjusted based on the performance of the underlying investment. Variable rate securities with no floor rate use the respective benchmark rate in all cases.
citations.where: Schedule of Investments notes following March 31, 2026 schedule

rationale: The filer does not present one all-in rate with a PIK-included footnote. Instead, footnote (b) says variable-rate securities bear interest at a base rate plus a basis point spread, and the same note separately defines PIK. The schedule rows confirm that the spread/rate and PIK are separately printed: variable-rate PIK rows show the spread first with PIK appended, while PIK-only fixed instruments print the percentage followed by PIK. Therefore the stated position-level rate/spread excludes separately quoted PIK unless the rate itself is explicitly marked PIK.
